title: Rainforest Layers
keyIdea: A rainforest has four layers. From the ground up, they are the forest floor, the understory, the canopy and the emergent layer. The floor is dark and damp, with rotting leaves. Small trees and bushes grow in the shady understory. The canopy is a thick roof of treetops, and most animals live there because it has light, fruit and leaves. The tallest trees poke above it into the bright emergent layer.
familyTip: Stand at the bottom of the stairs and call it the forest floor, then climb and name each layer: understory, canopy, emergent. Ask which animal might live on each step, and whether it would be dark or bright there.

visual.caption: High up or low down? Drag each card into a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: a sloth in the thick treetops
a harpy eagle on the tallest tree
monkeys eating fruit in the sun

lab.caption: Flagship lab: stack the four layers from the ground up, climb from dark to bright, put animals and plants in their layer, and drop leaves to rot on the floor.

kid: A rainforest is like a very tall house with four floors. From the ground up, they are the forest floor, the understory, the canopy and the emergent layer.
The forest floor is at the bottom. It is dark and damp. Old leaves fall there and rot into soil. Ants and beetles live there.

The understory is next. Small trees and bushes grow in the shade. Above it is the canopy. The treetops touch like a thick green roof. Most animals live in the canopy, because it has sun, fruit and leaves to eat.
The emergent layer is the very top. A few giant trees poke out above the canopy into bright sun and wind. Eagles sit there. The canopy is not the top. The emergent trees are higher.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. This supports Year 2 Living things and their habitats in the National Curriculum in England (most living things live in habitats to which they are suited) and NGSS 2-LS4-1 (observe plants and animals to compare the diversity of life in different habitats). It builds on What Is a Rainforest? and leads into food chains and how animals are adapted to where they live.

The four layers are named from the ground up: forest floor, understory, canopy, emergent. Light drops sharply from top to bottom, because the canopy leaves catch most of the sunlight. That is why the floor is dark and damp and why most rainforest animals live in the canopy, where food and light are greatest.

Common mistakes: thinking the canopy is the top layer, when the emergent trees stand above it. Mixing up the understory and the canopy, so the shady layer is called the roof. Picturing the forest floor as bright and hot. And thinking fallen leaves just pile up, when they rot quickly into soil.

In the lab your child builds the layers from the ground up and climbs a tree to see the light change. They tap a layer for each animal and count where most live. Then they drop leaves to rot on the floor, and match plants to their layer.

practice.prompt: Which layer of the rainforest is the very top?
practice.hint: Some giant trees poke out above the thick roof of treetops.
practice.explain: The emergent layer is the top. Its giant trees poke out above the canopy roof into bright sun.

practice.hint: The leaves above catch most of the sunlight.
practice.explain: Very little sun gets down to the forest floor, so it is dark and damp, with rotting leaves.

practice.prompt: In one rainforest, the canopy roof is 40 metres up. An emergent tree is {a} metres tall. How many metres does it stick out above the canopy?
practice.hint: Take the height of the canopy roof away from the height of the tree.
practice.explain: {a} take away 40 is {=a-40}. The tree pokes {=a-40} metres above the canopy, into the emergent layer.

practice.prompt: You count {a} animals in the canopy and {b} animals on the forest floor. How many more live in the canopy?
practice.hint: Take the smaller number away from the bigger number.
practice.explain: {a} take away {b} is {=a-b}. More animals live in the canopy, where there is sun, fruit and leaves.

practice.prompt: Small trees and bushes that grow in the shade are in the…
practice.hint: It is the layer just below the thick roof of treetops.
practice.explain: The understory is under the canopy roof, so it is shady. Small trees and bushes grow there.

pool.prompt: Where do most rainforest animals live?
pool.hint: Which layer has lots of sun, fruit and leaves?
pool.explain: Most animals live in the canopy, because it has the most light and food.

pool.prompt: Which order goes from the ground up?
pool.hint: The shady understory is under the canopy roof.
pool.explain: From the ground up: forest floor, understory, canopy, then the emergent trees on top.

pool.prompt: What happens to old leaves on the forest floor?
choices: they rot and turn into soil
they stay the same for ever
they blow back up to the trees
pool.hint: Think about what fungi and minibeasts do to dead leaves.
pool.explain: Fungi and minibeasts break the leaves down. They rot into soil that feeds the plants.

pool.prompt: A sloth hangs in the thick roof of treetops. Which layer is it in?
pool.hint: The treetops that touch make a roof. What is that layer called?
pool.explain: The thick roof of treetops is the canopy, so the sloth is in the canopy.

pool.prompt: Why is the forest floor dark?
choices: the leaves above catch most of the sunlight
the sun never shines on rainforests
pool.hint: What is between the sun and the ground?
pool.explain: Rainforests get lots of sun, but the canopy leaves catch most of it, so little light reaches the floor.

pool.prompt: A monkey climbs {a} metres up from the forest floor. The canopy roof is 40 metres up. How many more metres must it climb to reach the roof?
pool.hint: How far is it from {a} up to 40?
pool.explain: 40 take away {a} is {=40-a}, so it must climb {=40-a} more metres to reach the canopy roof.

pool.prompt: A toucan sits on the canopy roof, 40 metres up. It hops down {a} metres to a lower branch. How high up is the branch?
pool.hint: Start at 40 and take away the {a} metres it hopped down.
pool.explain: 40 take away {a} is {=40-a}, so the branch is {=40-a} metres up. Going down means lower, closer to the dark forest floor.

pool.prompt: A harpy eagle sits on top of the tallest tree, above all the others. Which layer?
pool.hint: Which layer pokes up above the canopy roof?
pool.explain: The tallest trees poke above the canopy into the emergent layer, so the eagle is there.
